newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--Port of NY/NJ pricing Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--Port of NY/NJ pricing Friday.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended down 1/8 to 1/4 point in light trade Thursday, while Lehman Brothers said it plans price $932 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey bonds Friday.
A municipal analyst said muni cash overall closed down 1/8 to 1/4 point.

High-grade issues worsened by two basis points, with the short end exhibiting greater weakness. Dollar bonds closed down 1/4 point. Activity was light, and new issue pricing was firm, the analyst said.
A municipal trader saw a slightly broader range of weakness.
"We're off a little, I would say anywhere from 1/8 to 3/8 of a point," he said.
The trader also observed a growing disparity between primary and secondary market levels.

"The market is kind of getting two tiered, where the secondary market is trading a little rich to the primary," he said. "What's happening is the deals are getting priced to go away, so there is very little in the Street. The Street is realizing that, so they are paying up a little bit."
The trader added that while primary deals look attractive, "you can't get any bonds unless you are an institution."
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 17/32 at 93-25/32 to yield 7.13 percent. Buyers stayed sidelined, letting prices slowly erode throughout the session, analysts said.

Participants said next week's busy calendar of significant economic events, remarks by Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer and this week's substantial new supply conspired to push government securities prices lower.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed down 11/32 at 112-9/32. The June T-bond contract closed down 13/32 at 107-10/32. The MOB spread was 159 ticks.
